items.description: Ruling D1's two premises are proven by the first app's phase on a real Jenkins build before the other apps follow: that build's validation Job pod reached Playwright's browser download host and downloaded Chromium, and the app's frontend built and tested on Node 24. The first app's done-record names the build.
items.rationale: The first app was ZigbeeControl (P6, `0a2c4a9`), build ZigbeeControl/ZigbeeControl #60, SUCCESS, named in plan.md's P6 done-record, which was pushed before P7-P9. Both premises hold. (1) Chromium was downloaded in the Job pod: the image carries no browser (P1 record: Playwright OS deps only, `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1`), so the frontend Playwright suite can only have passed by downloading it; Jenkins' test report has 50 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped, the same 50 as #59 on modern-app-dev-playwright. The done-record cites `cdn.playwright.dev` and Chrome for Testing 148.0.7778.96 from `validation.log`; I could not re-read that artifact (anonymous access is refused, HTTP 403), and the Job pod's logs have aged out. DHCPApp #49, ElectronicsInventory #255 and IoTSupport #145 then repeated it on the same image. (2) The frontend built and tested on Node 24: the Job's frontend suite (37 of #60's 50 tests) passed on the image, whose Node is v24.21.0 (`node --version` in the `modern-app` sidecar, which runs the same image; the done-record cites the Job's `vite build` from `validation.log`). The `vite v7.3.1` lines in #60's console belong to the later kaniko image build, not to the Job, so they are not this evidence.

items.description: DockerImages' `docs/registry-management/` carries the short procedure ruling D3 names: a repository's tags deleted through the registry API and its entry removed from registry storage, with no manual garbage collect. The procedure matches the registry as RegistryDeploy deploys it (storage backend, delete setting).
items.rationale: `docs/registry-management/delete-repository.md` (a963dfd, on DockerImages origin/main) carries the procedure: (1) HEAD every tag and `DELETE` each distinct digest through `http://registry:5000`, every response `202`; (2) `kubectl exec` into the `app=registry` pod in `registry-prd` with the prd-write kubeconfig and `rm -rf` the repository's directory; (3) confirm the repo is out of `/v2/_catalog?n=1000`; no garbage collect. It matches the registry as RegistryDeploy deploys it: the chart's `registry-deployment.yaml` has label `app: registry` (:9,13), image `registry{{ .Values.images.registry }}` (:19), the volume mounted at `/var/lib/registry` (:31) from `claimName: registry-pvc` (:49), i.e. filesystem storage. The read paths of step 1 work against the live registry: from this pod `tags/list` returns `modern-app-dev`'s 11 tags and `modern-app-dev-playwright`'s 2, and `_catalog?n=1000` lists both. That manifest deletes are enabled is P12's evidence (registry-cleanup's jobs logged 232 and 235 `Deleted` with no `Failed to delete`); I did not issue a DELETE. The step-2 and step-3 `REPO` guard is on the file.

Every DELETE returned 202, tags/list returned null, the three directories were removed from the registry pod's /var/lib/registry, and _catalog?n=1000 lists none of them.
